editorText:
The metallic clang of a transport pod coupling with the airlock bay shattered the mess's still silent hum. The sound reverberated through the hull of the Ignotius, dissipating as soon as they had arrived. Ripples atop John’s lifeless coffee faded away.

“The doctors’ transport pod” Kitten announced breaking the silence. “he just arrived from his station on the surface”.

John’s senses sharpened. Across the table, Tex stopped spinning his fork, setting it down beside his spotless plate, which he’d meticulously licked clean. Footsteps echoed from the corridor—familiar in a way that tugged at a buried memory within John. His pulse quickened. He had heard those footsteps before, in a dream, just before the briefing on the lost facility. But this time, there were two sets: one heavy, deliberate, and the other lighter, more cautious.

The Ignotius drifted in the void like a giant squid, silent, as the crew exchanged uneasy glances, waiting for what was to come.

“Doctor.. are these the Protectant you spoke of”, The confused stares of John and his team dissipated as another sentient companion Doc into the room. However, something about this Sentient was different. Tex could only just put his finger on it. “Is it just me or does this thing actually have hips?” He thought to himself.

“I have prepared an overview of the drilling superstructure embedded beneath the ice on Europa” Serra stepped forward emerging from the bulkheads behind Wolfgang, her shoulder sat proudly next to the Doctors, and eyed Tex directly with a soft conservative smile.

"Serra designed the facility herself: She ... was a board member on the Europa exploration team. head architect." The Doctor gave praise in his statement. "We worked together to test the viability of the worker bots in the high radiation of Europa's surface." Serra stepped forward she could tell Tex was the most uncomfortable about her sudden emergence into the room, although she put it down to sexual tension internally, he was just shy and she saw straight through it. "As well as pressure testing for the depth. My role was crucial in designing the hyperbaric chambers in a way that could convert the hydrogen to cells for the worker bot program” The Doctor announced “Nova was extraordinary in her field!” with a tone of excitement, that filled Tau with joy, Tau really liked her, and you could see it in the way she rested a keen eye across her visor flickering with eagerness as she spoke.

To Shai Serra invoked a sense of a lost kindred mother, hidden beneath the wires. She found it hard to fathom the kind of knowledge she would have accessed this past 150 years. Shai leant over to Tau perching respectfully behind her ear and in an instant whispered softly “I like this one”. Tau met her comment with a smile, Shai immediately spotted her dimples and met with a cute contained giggle.

“I am sure you and Shai will get along just fine”, Doc drew his attention from Serra to Shai, gesturing at Shai with his human like hand. “Shai is our Deep Space Medic Technician, if something goes wrong medically work with her in any extractions that may occur”. Serra’s template emoted what looked akin to a smile. “You must update me on the progress of the genetic tree printing bio-gel after this briefing Shai, I would be interested in your abstract around Neural flexibility in this new field”. Tex raised his eyebrows, with a slightly impressed tone but shying on impatience. “I am sure you will have plenty of time to get acquitted after the mission brief”. John gently redirected the attention of the room while nodding respectfully at the Doctor.
